title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page lists the data needed for an abstract, coefficient-general de Rham theorem 'by integration over simplices'. It continues the previous page, where a cosimplicial divided-power dg algebra A^*_* over a pd ring S (built from Γ^*(Φ) ⊗ ΛΨ modulo (T−t)_pd) is shown to carry a 'system of Stokes–De Rham integrals'.

Data:
(1) A cosimplicial differential graded k-algebra A_* = (A_n^*)_{n≥0}, augmented by ε: k → A_*^*. It carries a family K = (K_n), K_n : A_n^n → k, of 'integrals'. These satisfy Stokes' formula: K_n∘d equals the alternating sum of K_{n−1}∘(face restrictions). They are normalised by K_0∘ε_0 = id. Model case: polynomial or smooth forms on the standard simplices, with K_n = ∫_{Δ_n}.
(2) On a space X, a sheaf of dg algebras Ω^* that resolves the constant sheaf k_X. Model: the C^∞ de Rham complex of a manifold, k = R or C.
(3) A simplicial subset S(X)' ⊂ S(X) of the singular complex whose inclusion is a homology isomorphism. Model: smooth simplices. The marginal note upgrades this to a sheaf statement: the sheafified cochains S'_{X,k} should also be a resolution of k_X, like the full singular cochain sheaf S_{X,k}.
(4) For each σ ∈ S(X)'_n, a 'pull-back' σ^*: colim_{U ⊃ Im σ} Ω^*(U) → A_n^*. It must be compatible with every simplicial operator α: Δ_m → Δ_n, i.e. germ restriction followed by (σ∘α)^* equals σ^* followed by α^*_A.

Reformulation (NB): σ ↦ germs of Ω^* along Im σ is a presheaf of augmented dg objects on the simplex category of 𝒳 = S(X)'. Data (4) is then a morphism of augmented complexes over 𝒳 into the complex induced by A^*_*.

Final NB: (1) and (4) serve only to build the integration map Ω^* → S'^*_X, compatible with augmentations, by ω ↦ (σ ↦ K_n(σ^*ω)). Stokes makes this a chain map; K_0ε_0 = id gives compatibility with the augmentations from k_X. Since both sides resolve k_X, the map is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence de Rham cohomology ≅ singular cohomology with coefficients in k.

Purpose in the manuscript: the same formalism should apply with A_* the divided-power simplicial forms over a pd ring S. This would give an integral or pd 'Stokes–de Rham' comparison. The multiplicative properties are flagged on the previous page as still to be studied.
errors: A global homology isomorphism S(X)' → S(X) is not enough for the sheaf-theoretic argument. One needs the local statement that the sheafified S'-cochains form a resolution of k_X (true for smooth simplices on manifolds via local contractibility). The marginal note seems to add exactly this, so it is a gap Grothendieck himself patches.

Stokes' formula and the augmentation condition yield a chain map. To compare multiplicative structures (cup product vs wedge product) further data is needed, which Grothendieck acknowledges on the previous page ('propriétés multiplicatives').
Minor: the indexing is fluid between S'(X)_n and S(X)'_n, and between K_n: A_n → k and K_n: A_n^n → k.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'system of Stokes integrals' on an augmented cosimplicial dg algebra, used to produce a de Rham integration map to singular cochains
ideas.modern_name: Integration map from simplicial (Sullivan/Whitney/Thom) forms to cochains; Dupont's integration; the de Rham theorem via cosimplicial dga with fibre integration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney (1957), H. Cartan (Séminaire, 1950s, axiomatic de Rham), Sullivan (1977), Dupont (1976)

ideas.what: Sheaf-theoretic proof: both Ω^* and the sheaf of (smooth) singular cochains resolve k_X, and the integration map is a morphism of resolutions
Viewing σ ↦ germs of Ω^* along Im σ as a presheaf on the simplex category of S(X)', with a map to the cosimplicial algebra A_*
ideas.modern_name: Morphism of (pre)sheaves on the category of simplices; simplicial de Rham comparison

ideas.what: Intended application of this axiomatics to divided-power polynomial forms on simplices over a pd ring (previous page), giving integral/pd Stokes integrals
ideas.modern_name: Divided-power (integral) simplicial de Rham forms; cf. Cenkl–Porter integral forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl–Porter (early 1980s) for integral polynomial forms; pd crystalline techniques (Berthelot)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the de Rham integration theorem axiomatically for an arbitrary augmented cosimplicial dga with Stokes integrals over an arbitrary coefficient ring k. He intends to feed in the divided-power simplicial forms of the previous page. This anticipates the later development of integral/pd analogues of Sullivan's polynomial forms (Cenkl–Porter) and ties them to the pd (crystalline) de Rham complex, a link not usually attributed to him.
missed.quote: NB ... ①(A_X^*, k_X, K_X) et ④ ne servent que pour pouvoir définir Ω^* → S_X^* comp. avec augm.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models for cochains via divided-power forms remain of interest (integral rational/p-adic homotopy theory, comparison of crystalline and singular structures). This is a 1975–76 instance of the idea with pd structures built in, but the page itself only contains the routine axiomatic frame.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but standard axiomatization of the integration-over-simplices de Rham theorem. Its only interest is as the scaffolding for the divided-power version on the neighbouring page, which is the potentially less-known part.
transcription_corrections: 'K_X = (K_n)_{n≥0}' should probably read K = (K_n)_{n≥0} with K_n : A_n^n → k (degree-n part), satisfying Stokes and K_0 ε_0 = id.
In the last NB, 'π_X' is likely 'K_X' (the system of integrals), i.e. ①(A_X^*, ε_X, K_X).
's.dif.[?]' likely 's. dif.'/'satisf.' introducing the conditions {Stokes, K_0ε_0 = id}.
Marginal note roughly: 'donc il en résulte que le faisceau S'_{X,k} [des cochaînes sur S(X)'] est, comme S_{X,k}, une résolution de k_X'.
'complexe de Σ-modules' likely refers to modules over the simplex category of 𝒳 (i.e. presheaves on simplices), with k-augmentation.
